arxiv-2101-08570.title: Rapidity window dependence of ridge correlations in the glasma
arxiv-2101-08570.creator: Donghai Zhang, Yeyin Zhao, Mingmei Xu, Xue Pan, Yuanfang Wu
arxiv-2101-08570.description: Abstract We study ridge correlations of the glasma in pp collisions at s NN = 7 \sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=7 TeV by using the color glass condensate (CGC) formalism. The azimuthal collimation at long range rapidity is intrinsic to glasma dynamics and is reproduced here.

arxiv-2204-13154.title: Attention Mechanism in Neural Networks:
arxiv-2204-13154.creator: Derya Soydaner
arxiv-2204-13154.description: Abstract A long time ago in the machine learning literature, the idea of incorporating a mechanism inspired by the human visual system into neural networks was introduced. This idea is named the attention mechanism , and it has gone through a long development period. Today, many works have been devoted to this idea in a variety of tasks.

arxiv-2207-14563.title: On Asymptotically Locally Hyperbolic Metrics with Negative Mass This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Differential Geometry Inspired by Mathematical Physics in honor of Jean–Pierre Bourguignon for his 75th birthday. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGM
arxiv-2207-14563.creator: Piotr T. CHRUŚCIEL a and Erwann DELAY b
arxiv-2207-14563.description: Abstract We construct families of asymptotically locally hyperbolic Riemannian metrics with constant scalar curvature (i.e., time symmetric vacuum general relativistic initial data sets with negative cosmological constant), with prescribed topology of apparent horizons and of the conformal boundary at infinity, and with controlled mass. In particular we obtain new classes of solutions with negative mass.

arxiv-2307-01784.title: The Inner Sentiments of a Thought
arxiv-2307-01784.creator: Chris Gagne, Peter Dayan
arxiv-2307-01784.description: Abstract Transformer-based large-scale language models (LLMs) are able to generate highly realistic text. They are duly able to express, and at least implicitly represent, a wide range of sentiments and color, from the obvious, such as valence and arousal to the subtle, such as determination and admiration.

arxiv-2309-04275.title: Symmetries of exotic spheres via complex and quaternionic Mahowald invariants
arxiv-2309-04275.creator: Boris Botvinnik, J.D. Quigley
arxiv-2309-04275.description: Abstract . We use new homotopy-theoretic tools to prove the existence of smooth U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) - and S ​ p ​ ( 1 ) Sp(1) -actions on infinite families of exotic spheres. Such families of spheres are propagated by the complex and quaternionic analogues of the Mahowald invariant (also known as the root invariant).

arxiv-2401-15779.title: Value Sliced and Derivative Images for Source Mask in JWST MIRI Photometry
arxiv-2401-15779.creator: Y. Güray Hatipoğlu
arxiv-2401-15779.description: Abstract One of many ways for the James-Webb Space Telescope (JWST) to capture astronomical signals is the Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Imaging mode. To make this data ready for analysis, the JWST standard reduction pipeline has three stages and many mandatory and optional steps to produce analysis-ready data.

arxiv-2409-05491.title: A refined Frauchiger–Renner paradox based on strong contextuality
arxiv-2409-05491.creator: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, Stefan Weigert
arxiv-2409-05491.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, Stefan Weigert. The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other’s knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario.

arxiv-2410-11391.title: Benchmarking Data Efficiency in Δ \Delta -ML and Multifidelity Models for Quantum Chemistry
arxiv-2410-11391.creator: Vivin Vinod, Peter Zaspel
arxiv-2410-11391.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Vivin Vinod, Peter Zaspel. The development of machine learning (ML) methods has made quantum chemistry (QC) calculations more accessible by reducing the compute cost incurred in conventional QC methods. This has since been translated into the overhead cost of generating training data. Increased work in reducing the cost of generating training data resulted in the development of Δ \Delta -ML and multifidelity machine learning methods which use data at more than one QC level of accuracy, or fidelity.

arxiv-2410-16105.title: Addressing Spectral Bias of Deep Neural Networks by Multi-Grade Deep Learning
arxiv-2410-16105.creator: Ronglong Fang, Yuesheng Xu
arxiv-2410-16105.description: Abstract Deep neural networks (DNNs) have showcased their remarkable precision in approximating smooth functions. However, they suffer from the spectral bias , wherein DNNs typically exhibit a tendency to prioritize the learning of lower-frequency components of a function, struggling to effectively capture its high-frequency features. This paper is to address this issue.

arxiv-2502-00142.title: Open RAN Slicing with Quantum Optimization
arxiv-2502-00142.creator: Patatchona Keyela, Soumaya Cherkaoui
arxiv-2502-00142.description: Abstract RAN slicing technology is a key aspect of the Open RAN paradigm, allowing simultaneous and independent provision of various services such as ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), and massive machine-type communications (mMTC) through virtual networks that share a single radio access infrastructure.

arxiv-2503-16247.title: Update (October 2025): This version includes a Corrigendum after the Appendix, correcting reported results for ViM and NNGuide. Please refer to the corrigendum section for details and updated tables. OpenMIBOOD: Open Medical Imaging Benchmarks for Out-Of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2503-16247.creator: Max Gutbrod, David Rauber, Danilo Weber Nunes, Christoph Palm
arxiv-2503-16247.description: Abstract The growing reliance on Artificial Intelligence in critical domains such as healthcare demands robust mechanisms to ensure the trustworthiness of these systems, especially when faced with unexpected or anomalous inputs. This paper introduces the Open Medical Imaging Benchmarks for Out-Of-Distribution Detection, a comprehensive framework for evaluating out-of-distribution detection methods specifically in medical imaging contexts.

arxiv-2608-00356.title: The 1st AI Children Challenge
arxiv-2608-00356.creator: Boyi Li, Yifan Shen, Houze Yang, Xu Cao, Guojun Yun, Li Gao, Turong Chen, Long Xu, Jianguo Cao, Meihuan Huang

pmc-11477177.title: Endo-Aortic Clamping with the IntraClude® Device in Minimally Invasive Total Coronary Revascularization via Left Anterior Thoracotomy (TCRAT)
pmc-11477177.creator: Christian Sellin, Hilmar Dörge, Parwis Massoudy, Andreas Liebold, Robert Balan, Teruhiko Imamura, Maurizio Taramasso
pmc-11477177.description: Minimally invasive, sternum-sparing total coronary revascularization in multivessel disease via left anterior mini-thoracotomy (TCRAT) was introduced recently. Intra-aortic balloon occlusion is a conceivable option to avoid manipulation of the ascending aorta, to reduce the risk of stroke and to be able to treat patients with severe calcifications and unfavorable aortic anatomies.

pmc-11586093.title: A Modified Nickel Titanium Space Regainer Using an Open Coil Spring in a Pediatric Patient: A Case Report
pmc-11586093.creator: Sushmita Shan, Kavitha Swaminathan, Vivek K, SelvaKumar Haridoss, Kritiga Kumar
pmc-11586093.description: This case report introduces a novel modification in the space-regaining process using a nickel-titanium (NiTi) open coil spring in a five-year-old male patient with early primary molar loss. The space deficiency, which led to occlusal discrepancies such as posterior crossbite, was efficiently managed using the NiTi wire and open coil spring, which is known for its superelasticity.

pmc-11691948.title: SYMPTOM BURDEN AND RECURRENT FALLS IN OLDER CANCER SURVIVORS: A LONGITUDINAL POPULATION-BASED STUDY
pmc-11691948.creator: Myeongjin Bae, Kushang Patel, Nancy Gell
pmc-11691948.description: Older adults with a cancer history may be at greater fall risk as activity-limiting symptoms from cancer and cancer treatment often persist, even after treatment has ended. Therefore, we aimed to prospectively determine the effects of pain, fatigue, and sleep difficulty on fall risk in older adults with a cancer history.

pmc-12506487.title: Exploring CRISPR-Cas: The transformative impact of gene editing in molecular biology
pmc-12506487.creator: Vivek Pandey, Shivani Sharma, Yuba Raj Pokharel
pmc-12506487.description: This review traces the evolution of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) technology from a prokaryotic immune mechanism to a versatile tool for precise genome engineering. We compare CRISPR with traditional gene-editing methods like RNA interference (RNAi), zinc finger nucleases (ZFNs), and transcription activator-like effector nucleases (TALENs), emphasizing its advantages in target specificity, multiplexing, and ease of design.

pmc-13103584.title: Genotype-matched mapping reveals consistent regional flavour signatures and rhizosphere microbial correlates in spring-flush Yunnan large-leaf tea
pmc-13103584.creator: Jiayin Tong, Yunhan Li, Yanmei Zhang, Panpan Zhang, Kaibo Wang, Qian Zou, Shiquan Shen
pmc-13103584.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microbial correlates of tea terroir are often confounded by cultivar. Using eight SNP-confirmed genotype-matched pairs large-leaf tea cultivar pairs across Menghai and Pu’er, we tested whether rhizosphere communities covary with flavour chemistry during the spring flush. Under genotype control, the volatile Signature Index (VSI) was consistently higher in Menghai in all pairs, with a β-caryophyllene detection/non-detect contrast (7/8 detected in Pu’er vs 0/8 in Menghai).

pmc-13424412.title: Hyper-converged space-air-ground integrated low-altitude aerial vehicular networks: Architecture, challenges, and technologies
pmc-13424412.creator: Haibo Zhou, Jianzhe Xue, Yi Yuan, Zeyu Sun, Yunting Xu, Jiacheng Chen, Xuemin Shen
pmc-13424412.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this paper, we introduce the space-air-ground integrated low-altitude aerial vehicular networks (SAG-LAAVN) that deliver ubiquitous intelligent connectivity for three-dimensional intelligent transportation systems (ITS). Built upon an innovative hyper-converged architecture that unifies Data, Operation, Information, and Communication Technologies (DOICT), SAG-LAAVN aims to address the stringent connectivity requirements imposed by the rapid evolution of low-altitude aerial vehicles, offering seamless coverage, enhanced resilience, and improved quality of experience across diverse scenarios. Three key scientific challenges in the SAG-LAAVN are discussed.
